newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply higher on Sparks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply higher on Sparks.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed near the $10 per ton upper limit and soyoil futures were higher after Sparks Companies executive Willard Sparks forecast a rise in soybean futures, traders said.
"Well, Willard Sparks is in telling people how bullish everything is, and China is supposedly buying cargo after cargo of beans," said Jack Scoville, analyst with Price Futures Group in Chicago.
Sparks told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that CBOT soybean prices are set to rise sharply, especially in the nearby months, because of tight U.S. soybean stocks.
The U.S. Agriculture Department earlier this month put soybean ending stocks at a tight 125 million bushels.
Sparks' comments stirred ongoing concerns that tight soybean supplies won't last through the summer.
Rumors China was again looking to buy U.S. soybeans further rattled the market and suggested that recent price gains had not stifled world demand. U.S. exporters could not confirm the deal.
Soymeal ended $8.90 to $0.80 per ton higher with July up $8.10 at $286.80. Soyoil closed 0.27 to 0.13 cent per lb higher with July up 0.21 at 25.47.
The China rumors compounded supply concerns. With soybean stocks projected at a tight 125 million bushels, the trade has been wary of the rapid export pace.
USDA said marketing year-to-date soybean exports were at 744 million bushels as of last week, well ahead of the 647 million bushels shipped by that time last year.
Trade sources had expected U.S. exports to slow to a trickle as South American soybeans hit the market. But weekly export reports have not shown the slowdown.
Traders expected Thursday's USDA export sales report to show between 350,000 and 450,000 tonnes of soybeans shipped.

Floor sources noted last week's bidding war between soybean processors and exporters for what they perceive to be limited supplies. Cash basis levels shot up 15 cents per bushel in some U.S. Midwest areas last week.
Farmer selling of soybeans has been slow all season and a recent span of dry weather has allowed farmers to turn their attention to seeding new crop instead of selling old crop.
May soymeal drew further strength from the lack of deliveries against the May, although none had been expected. Conversely, heavy deliveries in soyoil capped gains.

On the day, funds bought at least 1,700 lots of soymeal. Refco Inc bought 300 lots December and 200 July, Prudential Securities bought 200 each July and December and ADM bought 300 May, 100 December and 200 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil, Smith Barney bought 600 lots July, Tenco Inc bought 300 July and FIMAT Futures bought 200 July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 35,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 32,066 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 29,000 lots, against Tuesday's 29,936.
